value: Ley 820 of 10 July 2003 sets the regime for leases of urban property used as housing (Arts. 1-2).
source_publisher: Ministerio de Vivienda, Ciudad y Territorio (Colombia)
note: Ley 820 de 2003 (urban housing leases), text as published by the Ministry of Housing (Spanish). Later amendments and court rulings were not checked. The Spanish text prevails.

value: A housing lease may be verbal or written; the parties must agree at least on identity, the property, price, rent, payment, term and similar points (Art. 3).
source_publisher: Ministerio de Vivienda, Ciudad y Territorio (Colombia)
note: Ley 820 de 2003 (urban housing leases), text as published by the Ministry of Housing (Spanish). Later amendments and court rulings were not checked. The Spanish text prevails.

value: A lease is deemed extended on the same conditions and for the same initial term if each party has met its obligations and the tenant accepts the rent adjustments allowed by the law (Art. 6).
source_publisher: Ministerio de Vivienda, Ciudad y Territorio (Colombia)
note: Ley 820 de 2003 (urban housing leases), text as published by the Ministry of Housing (Spanish). Later amendments and court rulings were not checked. The Spanish text prevails.

value: In urban housing leases the landlord may not demand cash deposits or other real security (cauciones reales) to guarantee the tenant's obligations, directly or through another person (Art. 16). A guarantee for utility bills may be required but may not exceed the value of the utility charges for the last 3 months (Art. 15).
source_publisher: Ministerio de Vivienda, Ciudad y Territorio (Colombia)
note: Ley 820 de 2003 (urban housing leases), text as published by the Ministry of Housing (Spanish). Later amendments and court rulings were not checked. The Spanish text prevails.

value: The monthly rent set by the parties may not exceed 1% of the commercial value of the property, and the commercial value for this purpose may not exceed twice the current cadastral value (Art. 18).
source_publisher: Ministerio de Vivienda, Ciudad y Territorio (Colombia)
note: Ley 820 de 2003 (urban housing leases), text as published by the Ministry of Housing (Spanish). Later amendments and court rulings were not checked. The Spanish text prevails.

value: After every 12 months at the same price the landlord may raise rent by no more than 100% of the CPI change in the previous calendar year, provided the new rent stays within the 1% cap; the landlord must tell the tenant the amount and the date it takes effect (Art. 20).
source_publisher: Ministerio de Vivienda, Ciudad y Territorio (Colombia)
note: Ley 820 de 2003 (urban housing leases), text as published by the Ministry of Housing (Spanish). Later amendments and court rulings were not checked. The Spanish text prevails.

value: Rent may be set in any currency but is paid in Colombian pesos at the market representative exchange rate on the date the obligation arose, unless the parties agree a different date or rate (Art. 19).
source_publisher: Ministerio de Vivienda, Ciudad y Territorio (Colombia)
note: Ley 820 de 2003 (urban housing leases), text as published by the Ministry of Housing (Spanish). Later amendments and court rulings were not checked. The Spanish text prevails.

value: Subject to Civil Code Art. 1993 and unless otherwise agreed, the tenant may deduct the cost of indispensable non-routine repairs from rent, but not more than 30% of the rent (Art. 27).
source_publisher: Ministerio de Vivienda, Ciudad y Territorio (Colombia)
note: Ley 820 de 2003 (urban housing leases), text as published by the Ministry of Housing (Spanish). Later amendments and court rulings were not checked. The Spanish text prevails.
